name: Jair
overview: Jair was a male member of the tribe of Manasseh noted in Scripture for capturing the region of Argob and naming it Havvoth-jair. His actions highlight a significant territorial conquest during the period of Israel's settlement in the Promised Land. Beyond this notable achievement, the biblical record provides limited additional personal details.
namesAndTitles: The name Jair means 'he gives light,' reflecting a proper Hebrew name without indication that it was given directly by God. This meaning may suggest a character associated with illumination or guidance, though the text does not elaborate further.
familyAndRelationships: Jair is identified as a descendant of Manasseh, anchoring his lineage within one of the tribes of Israel. It is also inferred from Scripture that Segub was his son, establishing a familial connection within the tribe. No other family relationships are explicitly recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Jair's significance lies primarily in his military and territorial achievements, as he secured the region of Argob and named it Havvoth-jair, marking Israelite expansion and settlement. This act demonstrates God's providence in granting the land to His people through their leaders. Jair's role, though briefly noted, contributes to the historical and tribal identity of Manasseh within the biblical narrative.
